title: What If a Lake Bigger Than Lake Erie Drained in Two Days?

scenes.text: What if a lake of 500 cubic miles drained in two days? One did.
Glacial Lake Missoula sat behind an ice dam, and its water was about 2,000 feet deep.
When the ice failed, the lake could empty in as little as 48 hours.
The flood raced across the Northwest at up to about 65 miles an hour.
It carved canyons and left debris across roughly 16,000 square miles.
Then the ice dam re-formed and it happened again, dozens of times over about 2,500 years.

description:
